newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cartel office discussions seen fading-Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: EU cartel office discussions seen fading-Van Miert.

text.p: Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday he thought a German proposal for a European independent cartel office would be short lived.
"I can say that it looks as if this idea is not going to be pursued," Van Miert told a seminar on competition policy organised by Brussels-based think-tank Centre for European Policy Studies.
The German Federal Cartel Office recently launched a campaign for the creation of a European competition authority that would be separate from the EU's institutions.

The idea is no more popular today than it was in the late 1980s when EU national governments agreed instead to give the Commission the power to examine all major mergers and acquisitions affecting the Union.
The head of the Italian anti-trust authority Giuliano Amato was previously reported to support Germany's proposal.
However, Van Miert said that Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi had ensured him in a recent meeting in Rome that the plan did not have Italy's backing.

He added that even in Germany some now wondered whether there was a need to discuss the issue at the EU's inter-governmental conference started earlier this year to revise the bloc's institutions ahead of enlargement to eastern Europe.
Van Miert said the Commission would fight the proposal tooth and nail as it saw no need for such a body.

He also questionned whether an hypothetical cartel office would be more or less independent from political interference, saying that even those who advocated the idea regularly tried to pressure the Commission on cases of their interest -- a thinly disguised reference to the EU-Germany fight over Volkswagen subsidies.
